    Key dates

    Backward plan from sign-in, recalculated from the NLD date. Wing planning deadlines, not regulation dates. Federal holidays and Thanksgiving week are stepped around.

    Goals

    Hundreds of CAP members meet with Congress on National Legislative Day. The aim is to inform Congress about CAP's volunteers, operations, and programs, with a focus on state and local impact. Each member's own story shows members of Congress how CAP serves the nation, the state, and thousands of communities.

    What participants learn

    • Leadership in a real setting
    • How the federal government works, first-hand
    • Teamwork
    • Communication: telling a short, true CAP story
    • Representing CAP and the wing

    Who goes

    • Selection: Cadet Programs nominates active members who take part in wing activities and represent the wing well. Notice goes by email.
    • Size:
    • Fitness: expect long walks around Capitol Hill and DC (several miles a day). Anyone who cannot walk that far should tell the Activity Director early so arrangements can be made.

    Schedule

    Subject to change. Hill meeting times are set when each office confirms. UOD is uniform of the day.

    Lodging

    One cadet in each room is the room lead. Room lists build from the participant file (see People and rooms).

    Equipment

      Transport

      The group drives to and from DC and uses Metro inside DC. Drivers swap at every stop; no one drives more than about 3 hours in a stretch. Gas stops take only the time needed to fuel.

      Metro trips

      Metro boarding order, every station and every train

      1. Lead senior member enters or boards first.
      2. Cadets follow.
      3. Trail senior member enters or boards last.

      Fare cards are handed out just before each turnstile and collected right after it, on entry and exit.

      Safety brief · , at sign-in

      Metro

      Stay behind the granite edge and its lights until the train stops and the doors open. Let riders off first. Step over the gap. Never block, force, or lean on doors. No running, no eating or drinking, no sitting on the platform edge or escalator handrail.

      If someone falls onto the tracks: do not go after them. Use the platform emergency intercom and call for help. If you fall, stay clear of the third rail and get into the recess under the platform edge. Do not lie down between the rails.

      Long drive and weather

      Seatbelt on the whole trip; the lap belt stays across your waist. Headphones for any sound. Ask before touching anyone or taking food or gear that is not offered. Do not wake sleepers unless a senior member asks. In bad weather, keep quiet so the driver can focus; we pull over if it is unsafe.

      Street crossings and crowds

      Cross only at signals, as one group, behind a senior member. No phones while walking. Know the day's rally point. If you are separated, stay where you are, call a senior member, and wait.

      Food allergies

      Report every allergy on your forms. Do not eat food you cannot identify. Do not share food.

      Load participant file to list reported allergies.

      Crime

      Stay together. Keep your wingman in sight. Wallet in an inside pocket. If robbed, hand it over. Lock the room door. After the senior member room check, no one leaves the room unless there is an emergency.

      Lodging

      Find the two nearest exits when you check in. Adults and cadets room apart. Senior members do room checks in pairs. Keep your door locked.

      Political conduct

      Do not engage with demonstrations. In uniform, do not endorse or criticize any party, candidate, or commentator, and do not give opinions on political issues. Tell your CAP story; that is the job.

      Who to tell

      Your wingman, then your room lead, then a senior member. Use the group's agreed messaging platform.

      Load participant file for senior member phones.

      Packing list

      Backpack (18 x 14 x 8.5 in)

      • Things to pass the drive: book, phone, tablet, games, notebook. Anything with sound needs headphones.
      • Power bank and chargers
      • One pack of moleskin
      • Water bottle
      • Umbrella
      • Warm coat (worn, not packed)
      • Medications

      Suitcase

      • Class A uniform: blouse, tie and tie tack or tab, service coat (only if you own one), all accoutrements, slacks or skirt, belt, flight cap (no service caps)
      • Black dress socks or nylons
      • Black dress shoes you can walk miles in
      • Khaki pants
      • Pajamas
      • Sneakers
      • Toiletries
      • 2 sets of comfortable travel clothes
      • 4 pairs of socks

      Separate bag

      • Warm blanket for sleeping and the van (sheets are provided)
      • Pillow
      • Snacks and drinks for the van (check the allergy brief)

      Money

      • Lunches, some dinners, and souvenirs

      Leave at the hotel

      • Knives and multitools, aerosol cans, and anything sharp: Capitol and office building security will stop them

      After action review

      Participants rate each item 1-5 (1 strongly disagree, 5 strongly agree), then name one part of the trip they really enjoyed and one thing to change next year.

      Overall

      1. The trip met its goals (leadership, networking, education).
      2. The trip was well organized.
      3. The trip was a valuable experience.
      4. I would recommend this trip.

      Logistics

      1. Transport was efficient and on time.
      2. Rest stops were well spaced.
      3. Lodging was good enough.
      4. There was enough time for rest, meals, and downtime.
      5. The schedule was reasonable, not exhausting.

      Safety

      1. The safety brief was clear.
      2. I felt safe the whole trip.
      3. Headcounts and check-ins worked.

      Meetings and events

      1. Meetings with members of Congress and staff were engaging.
      2. I felt prepared to talk with officials.
      3. The reception was worth attending.
      4. We had time to take part without rushing.

      Experience

      1. Everyone stayed professional and met CAP standards.
      2. Leaders and participants communicated well.
      3. There was a good balance of structure and downtime.
      4. The debrief covered the key takeaways.

      Food

      1. There was enough food.
      2. The food was good quality.
      3. Meal stops were good choices.
      4. There was enough time to eat.
      5. There was enough water.

      Side trips

      1. The Capitol tour added value.
      2. Each side trip was worth the time.
      3. Side trips supported CAP's aerospace education or citizenship goals.

      Next year

      1. The travel schedule should change.
      2. Leader communication could improve.
      3. Time per event was right.
      4. More preparation would have helped.

      Lessons carried forward
